new_terms.definition: The compiler cache. It stores compile results and reuses them in later builds.
The program that installs and updates Rust toolchains.
The Haskell build tool. It builds the ingest pipeline.
The Git hook runner. `lefthook.yml` lists the lint commands that it runs before a commit.
The TRON wrapper script that starts cargo. Inside the Nix dev shell it starts the cargo of the Nix Rust toolchain.
A generated file that `rust/rust-toolchain.sh` writes. `rust/run-cargo` sources it outside the Nix dev shell to select a Rust installation.
The Nix build that compiles TRON and its tests with CMake. `nix/cmake-tron-test-build.nix` defines it.
The Nix check that runs the CMake configure step of TRON inside the Nix build sandbox. `flake.nix` defines it.
The LLVM run-time checker that detects memory errors and memory leaks.
The CMake external project that builds include-what-you-use, a tool that checks `#include` lines.
A Google tool, version 1.5, that reads and writes hardware registers. A copy of its source and a built program are in `bin/iotools-1.5`.

notes: All 24 names are kept. Every evidence site was opened and every quote is on its line. Rows changed in meaning: ALL_PROXY, ARCHFLAGS, ASAN_OPTIONS, CARGO_HOME, CARGO_TARGET_DIR, CC, CCACHE_CONFIGPATH, CCACHE_DIR, CI, CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH. Three statements rest on tool behaviour that was measured on scratch files outside the checkout, with CMake 3.22.1 and GNU Make 4.3. First: a preset `environment` value replaces a caller value in `cmake --preset` and in `cmake --build --preset`, and `cmake --build <dir>` keeps the caller value. Second: `if(DEFINED ENV{...})` is true for an empty value. Third: `?=` in GNU Make keeps an empty value from the environment. The Nix dev shell has other versions of both tools. The measurement was not repeated there. ALL_PROXY: no code line shows that `httpx` reads the variable. `t/proxy/README.md` states it, and the effect cell names that file as the source. Two evidence quotes are a part of their source line: `nix/cmake-tron-test-build.nix:138` and `bin/ci/test_run_cargo_test_binary.py:194`. The whole lines contain the pipe character. The limit of 35 words for the external section is applied to every effect cell.

changes.now: bin/ci/test_run_cargo_test_binary.py:28, CMakeLists.txt:435, CMakeLists.txt:436

changes.name: CC
changes.was: The dev shells `default`, `tools` and `cuda` set the path of a `clang-19` wrapper. `cmake-sandbox` sets the clang of the Nix LLVM 19 package. `minimal` sets `clang-19`. The CMake presets set `CMAKE_C_COMPILER` to `clang-19` and do not name `CC`.
changes.now: The dev shells `default`, `tools` and `cuda` set the path of a `clang-19` wrapper. `cmake-sandbox` and the 2 Nix builds get the `clang` of the Nix LLVM 19 toolchain. `minimal` sets `clang-19`. The CMake presets set `CMAKE_C_COMPILER` to `clang-19` and do not name `CC`.
changes.why: The value at flake.nix:1164 belongs to `cmakeSandboxEnvironment`. The dev shell `cmake-sandbox` (flake.nix:1176-1177), the check `cmake-sandbox-configure` (flake.nix:1279-1280) and `tron-cmake-test-build` (flake.nix:1246) all share it. The old note named only the dev shell.

changes.name: CCACHE_CONFIGPATH
changes.was: `make` keeps a value from the caller and exports it to every recipe. ccache (the compiler cache) reads its configuration from this file.
changes.now: `make` keeps a caller value and exports it to every recipe. ccache (the compiler cache) reads its configuration from this file during `cmake --build`.
changes.why: The exported value acts in the build step only. The recipes run `cmake --build gen` with no preset (GNUmakefile:404), so the compile commands inherit the value that `make` exports (GNUmakefile:101-103). The configure recipe runs `cmake --preset` (GNUmakefile:657), where the preset value applies.

changes.name: CCACHE_CONFIGPATH
changes.was: The CMake preset `base-ninja` sets `${sourceDir}/.ccache/ccache.conf` for the configure step and replaces a caller value. The Nix build `tron-cmake-test-build` sets the file of its source copy when its shared cache directory is writable.
changes.now: A `cmake --preset` run with a preset that inherits `base-ninja` uses `${sourceDir}/.ccache/ccache.conf` and ignores a caller value. `bin/bsub-build` does not forward an environment value to the LSF job. The Nix build `tron-cmake-test-build` sets the file of its source copy when it uses ccache.
changes.why: The preset `darwin` does not inherit `base-ninja` (CMakePresets.json:41-55), so the replacement holds only for the other presets (CMakePresets.json:13-16, :35, :61, :88, :101, :113). `bin/bsub-build` forwards only 3 names and starts the job with `env -i` (bin/bsub-build:54, :65). The replacement of a caller value was measured on scratch files with CMake 3.22.1.

changes.name: CCACHE_DIR
changes.was: `make` keeps a value from the caller and exports it to every recipe. ccache (the compiler cache) stores and looks up compile results in this directory.
changes.now: `make` keeps a caller value and exports it to every recipe. ccache (the compiler cache) stores and looks up compile results in this directory during `cmake --build`.
changes.why: Same reason as `CCACHE_CONFIGPATH`: the exported value acts in the build step (`cmake --build gen`, GNUmakefile:404). The configure recipe uses the preset value (GNUmakefile:657, CMakePresets.json:15).

changes.name: CCACHE_DIR
changes.was: The CMake preset `base-ninja` sets `/tmp/ccache-$env{USER}` for the configure step and replaces a caller value. The Nix build `tron-cmake-test-build` sets `/opt/positron/.cache/ccache-nix` when that directory is writable. `bin/bsub-build` does not forward the variable to the LSF job.
changes.now: A `cmake --preset` run with a preset that inherits `base-ninja` uses `/tmp/ccache-$env{USER}` and ignores a caller value. `bin/bsub-build` does not forward an environment value to the LSF job. The Nix build `tron-cmake-test-build` sets `/opt/positron/.cache/ccache-nix` when that directory exists and is writable.
changes.why: The preset `darwin` does not inherit `base-ninja` (CMakePresets.json:41-55). The Nix build tests `-d` and `-w` (nix/cmake-tron-test-build.nix:104), so `exists and is writable` is the exact condition. A make command-line override does travel with the LSF job (GNUmakefile:394-399), so the note now says `environment value`.

changes.name: CI
changes.was: Any non-empty text counts as set. The text is not parsed. The CI workflows set `true`.
changes.now: Any non-empty text counts as set, also `0` and `false`. The text is not parsed. The CI workflows set `true`.
changes.why: Every reader tests only for a non-empty value: bin/scratch-dir.sh:108, GNUmakefile:1 and :856, flake.nix:1748, lefthook.yml:57. A person who types `CI=0` or `CI=false` gets the CI behaviour. The cell now says so.

changes.name: CI
changes.was: Any non-empty value marks a CI run. `bin/scratch-dir.sh` creates a plain build directory and no `/scratch` link. `lefthook` commands fail when a lint tool is missing. The Nix dev shell installs no Git hooks.
changes.now: When it is not empty, `bin/scratch-dir.sh` removes a link at the build directory and creates a plain directory. `lefthook` commands fail on a missing lint tool. The Nix dev shell hook installs no Git hooks.
changes.why: The old cell said `creates a plain build directory and no /scratch link`. The script also deletes an existing link first (bin/scratch-dir.sh:109: `[[ -L $dir ]] && rm -f -- "$dir"`). A person who sets `CI` in a developer checkout loses the link to the scratch build tree.

changes.name: CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH
changes.was: The root `CMakeLists.txt` checks it when it configures `iwyu_external` (the include-what-you-use external project). When it is defined, TRON passes no `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH` argument. The sub-build then inherits the variable.
changes.now: The TRON configure step tests whether it is defined. If so, TRON passes no `-DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH` argument to `iwyu_external` (the include-what-you-use external project). That sub-build then inherits the variable.
changes.why: The old text `checks it when it configures iwyu_external` placed the test in the sub-build. The test runs when CMake reads the root file (CMakeLists.txt:622-624), and the result is stored in the arguments of `ExternalProject_Add` (CMakeLists.txt:637-646).
